[b]The Offices of Alexander Mekedii:  March 5th, 2025[/b]

 As the Chamber of the Peoples met that morning to discuss the future of her husband and of Tito Alexandrii, Lady Theodora took advantage of the fact that the Senate was not in session to make good on her decision to meet with the young Senator Mekedii, as she had discussed with Doma. Arriving discreetly by car to the offices of the Senators, which were connected to the Basilica of the Peoples she adjusted her gown and veil which covered her face. It was tradition for ladies of Adní to veil themselves, her unique position as one married made it so that the veiling wasnt required, but she still did so.

Stepping out of the car she made her way up the grand steps of the underground entrance to the Basilica, being greeted by the guard at the door who let her into the grand building. Carrying a purse with her she looked the picture of elegance, her ankle length dress swaying with every step along the marble floors of the structure. 

Alexander was not expecting visitors, that much she had surmised, Senators rarely received visitors beyond members of the Chamber of the Peoples, as such she expected little resistance to their meeting. Making her way along the hallways of the Basilica, she paused to look at a livestream of the chamber's proceedings, she smiled as she recognised her son near the front of the chamber, nodding along with the droning voices of the representatives. 

She finally tore her eyes away from the television and moved once more towards the offices of Alexander, being let in by his secretary.  She sat in the small waiting room that she had been directed to, it was surprisingly simple for one she knew to be so fiery in tongue, perhaps he hadnt thought to decorate, or was too busy being a firebrand to decorate. She smirked at this.

After an agonising thirty minutes Alexander finally appeared, dressed in a dark suit with a dull colored tie, his long blonde locks draped over the shoulders of the suit. Greetings lady Ptolenos, he stated as Theodora rose to greet him, presenting her gloved hand for him to kiss.

Greetings Senator, replied Theodora as he politely kissed her hand, and entered his office, which was a cluttered affair with papers piled high and overflowing out of boxes, books were scattered across tables and the couches in the room, it was at least more interesting than the waiting room. 

I do apologise for my tardiness madam, I had a meeting with some members of the chamber that ran over too long, stated Alexander seating himself.

Ah, replied Theodora, Well there is no harm in that, she stated, subtly flaunting her graces before Alexander.

Now what did you wish to meet with me about? It is unusual that a member of the Ptolenos should wish to meet with one so openly opposed to them, began Alexander, leaning forward. 

I am flexible Senator Mekedii when I must be, Replied Theodora, flashing a smile at him before continuing, But no, I have come here to offer you a deal, a partnership so to speak, she stated.

It is bold of you to assume, Lady Ptolenos, that I would take any deal from you, replied Alexander.

Yet you havent heard my offer, that is bad diplomacy, senator, replied Theodora, smiling slyly.

Well then, let us hear this, replied Alexander leaning back in his chair.

As you know senator, speaker Alexandrii-Claudis stands in a precarious position after yesterdays tie breaking vote, began Theodora as Alexander nodded along, Unfortunately, with his actions raising suspicions across the government, well, it seems likely that he might be removed, or forced to step down, she continued.

Yes, that is very true, and I wish the speaker all the best, but of course, his actions as you yourself have said are most precarious, replied Alexander affirming what Theodora had said.

Precisely, which is where you come in, replied Theodora, You see with his removal from the position, the Senate will most likely move to vote for a new speaker, and of course we need a strong speaker in the Senate to ensure stability, she continued as Alexander seemed to realise what she was hinting at.

So you are offering me the position? Is this right? Enquired Alexander.

Potentially, the president has enough connections to ensure you receive the baton, so to speak, stated Theodora.

Alexander smirked slightly before leaning forward, Lady Ptolenos, while I mean no disrespect, I do say that you are a terrible person, and to think that I would cast aside my loyalties to the people for mere power, well you underestimate my abilities, he stated, causing Theodora to drop her smile.

Perhaps you hold a poor view, or perhaps you misunderstand my motive here senator, I only seek the stability of the republic, and the people of this nation, replied Theodora, her face taking on a neutral expression as she shifted slightly in her seat.

Do you? Do you really seek the stability of this nation, or is that what your husband told you to say to me? Lady Ptoleny, I should ask that you leave my office, I reject your offer to your face, for it is clear that your husband sent you with your silken tongue to offer me bribery to remain silent and not oppose him, with offering of the sacred position of Speaker, no, I reject this offer, replied Alexander, his tone rising slightly. 

Theodora blinked slightly, attempting to gauge her potential response, she had expected him to accept or at least provide a counter offer, she put on her smile once more and replied with full delicacy, Perhaps I was not clear with my offer senator Merkedii, it is a form of protection, there are individuals who have heard your fiery tongue, and who seek to hurt you, or your family, she stated, her tone remaining gentle. 

Ha! A noble lie, nay, I reject this premise, no, perhaps you wish to harm my family, perhaps your husband, but nay, I reject this, if you have anything else to say, please say it elsewhere replied Alexander, moving to the office door and opening it, Have a good day, he stated as Theodora rose stiffly and walked out. 

She turned once more to look at him, but he quickly shut the door after her with a resolute click. The meeting had not gone as planned, however, Theodora knew that Alexander would act once the reality of the situation had been shown to him. She didnt wish to see the young man dead, nor his family injured or removed, yet if it was all she had left, she would bend there. 

Leaving the office and returning to the car she called Doma to arrange a formal meeting at her residence later in the day. She needed to pay a visit to her son Mikael.
